heading: Security Considerations
text: Keyring implementations SHOULD provide integrity guarantees for the encrypted data keys they return on OnEncrypt such that tampered versions of those encrypted data keys, if input into OnDecrypt, are overwhelmingly likely to cause a decryption failure (i.e. the chance of a successful decryption in this case is negligible).

heading: Security Considerations
text: Such integrity guarantees SHOULD include the integrity of the encryption context such that, if the encryption context used as input to OnEncrypt to produce an encrypted data key is different than the encryption context input to OnDecrypt to decrypt that encrypted data key, the decryption is overwhelmingly likely to fail.

heading: Security Considerations
text: Users SHOULD use a keyring that protects wrapping keys and performs cryptographic operations within a secure boundary.

heading: Appendix > Why should I use Keyrings instead of Master Key Providers and Master Keys?
text: Due to this simplified architecture, master keys and master key providers are going to be deprecated in the future, and new implementations SHOULD use keyrings.

text: - Encryption Context MUST be constructed by Custom Encryption Context From Authenticated Encryption Context

heading: Record Format > Custom Encryption Context From Authenticated Encryption Context
text: For every key in the encryption context the string `aws-crypto-ec:` + the UTF8 decode of this key MUST exist as a key in the authenticated encryption context.

heading: Record Format > Custom Encryption Context From Authenticated Encryption Context
text: Also, the value in the encryption context for this key MUST equal the value in the authenticated encryption context for the constructed key.
